analysis.title: Global Economics Daily Points, October 28, 2026
key_insights: Markets are over 80% priced for a Bank of Canada hike today, and five of the six major Canadian banks expect one. The BoC statement and MPR arrive at 9:45am ET and the press conference at 10:30am ET.

Scotia sees three possible BoC bias scenarios. Macklem stays cagey and noncommittal on forward guidance, or he hikes and leans mildly hawkish on upside inflation risk while trading trade shocks against commodity shocks, or he returns to the staff's April 'illustrative scenario with persistently higher energy prices' and its guidance that consecutive increases would be required.
The hawkish BoC scenario would spike December pricing and probably January pricing, and the front-end would sell off sharply.

Client discussions on the BoC: 25% totally onside with a hike and further hikes, 10% totally disagree, 40% somewhat disagree with the amount priced, 25% sidelined lacking conviction. No clients expect more hikes than priced and none expect cuts.
Scotia's BoC forecast is a harder sell to clients because the market has moved close to its view, so the author is wary of advising more risk on expected hikes while awaiting evidence.
Markets are about 90% priced for a Fed hold today and a hike in December. The FOMC statement is at 2pm ET and Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30pm ET. No SEP is due until December 9.

The September FOMC dot plot indicated one more hike in 2026Q4 and then unchanged through 2027. A Fed hike today would be a major shock and would add to December hike pricing regardless of the dot plot.

Warsh dislikes forward guidance. Markets read his IMF-meeting comments ('I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings we have in the balance of this year') as dovish, which the author finds puzzling.

Scotia estimates core PCE at +0.4% m/m SA, released tomorrow, which would be relatively warm. A hike would rattle markets days before the midterms and add to doubts about the Chair's reaction function.

RBA pricing for the November decision rose from about 15bps to 21bps of a quarter-point move after Australian CPI and hawkish testimony from Governor Bullock and colleagues, who said recent inflation readings were too high and hotter than their August outlook.
Australian Q3 CPI was 4.3% y/y vs 4.2% consensus. Trimmed mean was 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% consensus and 1.0% q/q, in line. September CPI was 0.8% m/m vs 0.7% consensus.

The RBNZ unexpectedly held at 2.75% when markets priced almost a full 25bps hike. The vote was 4-3 to hold vs hike, following 50bps of prior hikes. NZD fell and the kiwi front-end rallied, partly offset by guidance that further tightening was probably needed.
Chile's central bank held at 4.5% as expected with a hawkish bias, flagging rising inflation risks.
Alphabet and Microsoft report after the close. The UK Autumn Budget is at 8:30am ET, with early reports that the expected bank tax hike may be smaller than expected.

Upcoming event load: US midterms next Tuesday, Canada's Budget next Thursday, and US and Canadian jobs reports next Friday. Israel's election count (70.6% counted) has Netanyahu's bloc slightly ahead.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: a hike plus a return to the staff's persistently higher energy price scenario with consecutive increases would spike December and January pricing. Five of six major Canadian banks expect a hike.
tension_points.bear_case: 40% of clients somewhat disagree with the amount priced, 10% disagree with tightening at all, and Scotia notes the market has already moved close to its forecast.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cagey, noncommittal Macklem with no hawkish bias in the statement, MPR and press conference.

tension_points.bull_case: A warm core PCE (Scotia estimates +0.4% m/m) and the September dot plot showing another 2026Q4 hike support December hike pricing.
tension_points.bear_case: Other FOMC officials have downplayed a hike at this meeting, and markets read Warsh's no-guidance comments as dovish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core PCE print well below the +0.4% m/m estimate, or a statement and press conference that abandon the tightening bias.
